prerequisites: Basic principles of Chemistry: atomic structure

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the necessary basics of solid-state physics to understand and describe the operation of present and future semiconductor devices.
Acquire physical insight into the properties of semiconductors.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Basic principles of quantum mechanics
Periodic structure of crystalline solid state
Part 1: Crystal periodicity and symmetry properties of crystal structures
Part 1: Schrödinger equation : consequences of crystal symmetry
Part 2: Properties of the band structure of solids
Part 1: Equilibrium distribution functions : Fermi and Bose-Einstein
Part 2: Doping in semiconductors and density of states
Part 3: Electron and hole densities : the Fermi level
Part 1: Motion of electrons in a crystal : the effective mass theorem/approximation
Part 2: Semiclassical theory of electron dynamics in solids
Exercises sessions for each major theoretical topic
assessment_rules: The exam takes place during the examination period. It consists of open and closed questions. 50% of the exam consists of exercises (closed questions), and 50% consists of theory (open questions). Exercises are open book, while theory is closed book.
bibliography: Copy of the slides used during the lectures.
Fundamentals of Solid-State Physics for Semiconductors, G. Willems, R. Van Overstraeten, H.E. Maes, 3e edition, Acco, 1995
Exercise descriptions will be provided on Toledo.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
